$comment: Curated 'classic interconnects': product pairings the industry simply expects to work together (payments↔accounting, chat↔issue tracking, repo↔deploys…). This file asserts NOTHING about whether an integration exists — each entry's `expectation` says why people expect the pairing, and /integrations renders every pair with its live status computed against the verified evidence graph (lib/integrations.ts): 'verified' when an evidence-backed edge exists, otherwise the honest 'no evidence found yet' (which doubles as the evidence-coverage to-do list). Ids must be tracked products; validated by lib/classicPairs.ts (zod) + lib/__tests__/classicPairs.test.ts (ids exist, no dupes, no self-pairs).

pairs.expectation: Stripe payouts and fees reconciled into QuickBooks is the default books setup for online businesses.
Stripe is a first-class payment service in Xero — invoices paid by card land in the ledger automatically.
Shopify Payments is built on Stripe rails; Stripe checkout behind a storefront is the canonical e-commerce stack.
PayPal has been a stock Shopify checkout option since the platform's early days.
Turning a Slack thread into a Linear issue is the pairing's signature move — modern issue tracking lives next to chat.
Jira notifications and issue creation in Slack channels is the default enterprise dev-team setup.
PR and deploy notifications in a Slack channel are table stakes for any software team.
Salesforce owns Slack; deal-room channels wired to CRM records are the flagship of that acquisition.
Notion page previews and updates in Slack are the standard docs-next-to-chat wiring.
Slack is perennially among Zapier's most-connected apps — the default automation target for notifications.
PagerDuty alerts paging an on-call channel in Slack is the canonical incident-response loop.
Datadog monitors alerting into Slack channels is the standard observability notification path.
Creating and updating Asana tasks from Slack has been a headline integration for both products for years.
HubSpot deal and ticket notifications in Slack are the standard SMB revenue-team setup.
Push-to-deploy from a GitHub repo is Vercel's core workflow — the integration is the product.
Netlify's git-based continuous deployment from GitHub defined the Jamstack workflow.
Linear issues auto-linking and closing from GitHub PRs is one of Linear's most-used integrations.
Smart commits and branch links between GitHub and Jira are the classic enterprise dev-tracking bridge.
Sentry linking errors to GitHub commits/PRs and opening issues is the canonical error-tracking wiring.
Snyk scanning GitHub repos and PRs for vulnerable dependencies is its flagship developer workflow.
GitLab commits and MRs referencing Jira issues is a long-standing enterprise pairing.
Embedding live Figma frames in Linear issues is the standard design-to-build handoff.
Figma embeds in Notion docs are the default way design specs live in a team wiki.
Zapier writing rows into Notion databases is the standard no-code automation for Notion workspaces.
Sending DocuSign envelopes from Salesforce opportunities is the archetypal CRM-to-signature flow.
Gusto payroll runs syncing to QuickBooks is the default small-business payroll-to-books setup.
Ramp card transactions syncing to QuickBooks is the spend-management category's core accounting promise.
Brex expenses exporting to QuickBooks is the standard startup card-to-books reconciliation.
Mercury bank feeds into QuickBooks are the expected startup banking-to-accounting wiring.
Square sales importing into QuickBooks is the classic point-of-sale-to-books integration for retail.
Datadog monitors triggering PagerDuty incidents is the canonical monitoring-to-on-call pipeline.
Fivetran loading connectors into Snowflake is the archetypal managed-ELT-to-warehouse stack.
Segment streaming events into Amplitude is the classic CDP-to-product-analytics pipe.
Segment as the collection layer feeding Mixpanel is a founding use case of the CDP category.
